title: Open ball
parts: The points at distance strictly less than r from x.
note: The boundary is excluded from an open ball.
wrong: The points at distance at most r from x.
The points exactly r from x.

title: Closure of a set
parts: The smallest closed set containing A.
note: A closure includes A as well as all of its limit points.
wrong: The largest open subset of A.

title: Interior of a set
parts: The largest open set contained in A.
note: Whether a point is interior depends on the ambient space.
wrong: The smallest closed set containing A.
The set of all boundary points of A.

title: Boundary of a set
parts: The points whose every neighbourhood meets both A and its complement.
note: This ∂ marks a boundary. In calculus, ∂ also marks partial derivatives.
wrong: Every point in the interior of A.

title: Topological space
parts: The set X together with the topology τ specifying its open sets.
example: For X = {a,b}, τ = {∅,{a},X} is one possible topology.
note: The same underlying set can carry more than one topology.
wrong: The point X is at distance τ from the origin.
τ is a single open set inside X.

title: Preimage of a set
parts: All inputs whose images under f lie in U.
note: A preimage is defined even when f has no inverse function.
wrong: The reciprocal of each value in U.
All outputs obtained by feeding U into f.

title: Homeomorphic spaces
parts: In this topology context, X and Y are related by a continuous bijection with continuous inverse.
example: The intervals (0,1) and ℝ are homeomorphic via x ↦ log(x/(1−x)).
note: The symbol depends on context. Homeomorphic spaces need not have equal distances.
wrong: X and Y have identical points and distances.
There is only a continuous map from X to Y.

title: Tangent space
parts: The vector space of tangent vectors to manifold M at point p.
example: At the point (1,0) of the unit circle, tangent vectors are of the form (0,t).
note: The space is attached to a particular point p.
wrong: All points on M except p.
The vector space of positions of all points on M.
